# Controlled Autonomy Checklist: Agentic Software Engineering System: URL Shortener

**Purpose**: Validate that agent autonomy is bounded by declared permissions and that human-reserved actions are unreachable by agents.
**Created**: 2026-10-15
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [ADRs](../../../docs/adr/README.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.
**Item tags**: `[Mandatory]` means the criterion derives from the constitution, an approved requirement, or an accepted ADR or ruling. `[Optional]` means it concerns an enhancement. `[Dnn]` refers to a detection from the checklist brief; the detection map is in [../gates/release-evidence-gates.md](../gates/release-evidence-gates.md). Post-implementation evidence checks are in that gates file, not here. Every item is unchecked, including `[Optional]` items, so `/speckit-implement` reports this file as incomplete until a reviewer marks it.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are agent roles and their declared permissions specified for every agent stage? [Completeness, Spec §FR-ORC-025; workflow-graph.v2.yaml agent_roles] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK002 Is a closed list of human-reserved actions defined that cannot be granted to any agent role? [Clarity, Spec §FR-GOV-001, §FR-GOV-003; workflow-graph.v2.yaml] [D06] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the outcome of an out-of-permission agent action specified as refused and audited? [Coverage, Spec §FR-ORC-025, §NFR-AUT-001] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK004 Is refusal of agent-role API credentials specified for every human-reserved endpoint, with the refusal audited? [Completeness, Spec §FR-GOV-003, §SC-011] [D06] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK005 Are agent write boundaries (isolated workspace only, no repository writes) specified as permissions rather than conventions? [Completeness, Spec §FR-ORC-043; ADR-010] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK006 Is recording of the agent execution mode required per run, with AI-backed runs excluded from scenario evidence? [Completeness, Spec §FR-ORC-029] [D23] [Mandatory]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 Is enforcement required at both the HTTP layer and the engine layer, so that bypassing one layer is still refused? [Clarity, ADR-010; Spec silent] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK008 Is enabling AI-backed mode defined as an explicit configuration choice with a secure default of off? [Clarity, Spec §FR-ORC-030; Plan §8] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK009 Is it specified what an agent does on encountering ambiguity (return a clarification request) and what it must not do (proceed on a guessed interpretation)? [Clarity, Spec §SCN-C-AC5; ADR-017] [Mandatory]
- [ ] CHK010 Are fault-injection capabilities restricted to test configuration and to runs labeled `fault-injection`? [Clarity, Plan §10.3; ADR-018] [D23] [Mandatory]

## Ambiguities and Conflicts

- [ ] CHK011 Is the separation-of-duties rule (the same key identity may not both request and approve an exception, or approve its own request) specified with its refusal and audit outcome, and reconciled with A-008's multiple roles through different keys? [Completeness, Spec §FR-GOV-017 (CR-003), §A-008, §FR-GOV-008] [D10] [Mandatory]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- `[Gap]` = the requirement is missing; `[Ambiguity]` = the term or rule needs a definition; `[Conflict]` = two sources disagree; `[Assumption]` = relies on an unvalidated assumption
